    "CHEBI:176843": {
      "source_key": "chebi176843",
      "sha256": "b535c3de88f47e93aed8909c58ff4e2d054a6845dea3bc9a048c18df12b371a9",

      "properties": {
        "iri": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_176843",
        "lang": "en",
        "description": [
          "Any member of a group of cobalamin vitamers that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B&lt;small&gt;&lt;sub&gt;12&lt;/sub&gt;&lt;/small&gt; deficiency. Vitamin B&lt;small&gt;&lt;sub&gt;12&lt;/sub&gt;&lt;/small&gt; deficiency is associated with low red blood cell count and anemia. The vitamers are found in foods such as cereals, meat, fish, and poultry. The vitamers include adenosylcobalamin, hydroxocobalamin, cyanocobalamin, aquacobalamin, nitritocobalamin and methylcobabalamin (also includes their ionized, salt and phosphate derivatives)."
        ],
        "synonyms": [
          "vitamin B-12",
          "vitamin B12 vitamer",
          "vitamin B12 vitamers",
          "vitamin B12",
          "vitamins B12"
        ],
        "annotation": {
          "has_obo_namespace": [
            "chebi_ontology"
          ],

            "CHEBI:176843"
          ]
        },

      "properties": {
        "iri": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_17015",
        "lang": "en",
        "description": [
          "&lt;small&gt;D&lt;/small&gt;-Ribitol in which the hydroxy group at position 5 is substituted by a 7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[&lt;em&gt;g&lt;/em&gt;]pteridin-10(2&lt;em&gt;H&lt;/em&gt;)-yl moiety. It is a nutritional factor found in milk, eggs, malted barley, liver, kidney, heart, and leafy vegetables, but the richest natural source is yeast. The free form occurs only in the retina of the eye, in whey, and in urine; its principal forms in tissues and cells are as flavin mononucleotide and flavin-adenine dinucleotide."
        ],

### Repaired maintained owner and stale generated target

ownership: concern. Targets: CultureMech:010170.

The sole maintained owner is TOGO M763. Its September repair adds seven populated stock structures, correct source-specific hydrate IDs and staged preparation; the generated August target still has seven Unknown placeholders and older mass-labelled additions. The linked CultureMech:003081 JCM-derived record is related context, not a second owner. Preserve current repairs while revisiting their unsupported quantitative bases.

### Explicit glucose variant scope

quantity: supported. Targets: CultureMech:010170.

M763 comments[2] explicitly replaces 0.1 M L-sodium lactate with filter-sterilized 0.1 M glucose at 100 ml/L. The maintained owner correctly retains that strength and dose. This explicit per-litre instruction does not establish a final-volume denominator for every other ingredient or stock.

### Retained anaerobic ordering and bounded gaps

representation: concern. Targets: CultureMech:010170.

The maintained owner retains N2–CO2 80:20 v/v, sealed basal autoclaving, cooling and aseptic anaerobic stock additions; the target omits them. The source does not establish main incubation temperature, pH, pressure or autoclave duration. A pure-N2 sulfide-stock atmosphere and the owner statement that JCM 197 prints vitamins per litre are not supported by the scoped source wording.

### Supplied forms versus label spelling

grounding: concern. Targets: CultureMech:010170.

The receiving owner has correct hydrated Co/Ni IDs CHEBI:53503/53542, unlike the scoped M288 dependency. Its CuCl2 dihydrate and ZnCl2 IDs are chemically compatible, but four primary/secondary labels differ from canonical copper(II) chloride dihydrate and zinc dichloride. Generic calcium pantothenate and lipoic acid wording does not demonstrate a stereochemical conflict.

## Findings

### f1: Regenerated output must retain the maintained seven-stock repair

major / open / confirmed; issue key: m763-stale-generated-stock-topology.

The target still has empty Unknown stock compositions and mass-labelled additions, while the sole owner has seven populated stocks and preparation. Its generated resazurin 0.5 G_PER_L and water 830 G_PER_L also retain old units. The owner repair is real and must not be described as absent or flattened.

### f2: Retain repaired stocks while removing unsupported quantitative bases

major / open / confirmed; issue key: m763-owner-denominators-and-percent-bases.

The owner promotes batch masses, most stock additions and listed solvent to per-litre rates, treats bare 8%/5% as w/v, and scales phosphate masses by an assumed 100 ml final stock volume. Glucose 0.1 M at 100 ml/L is explicitly supported and is excluded from this denominator concern.

### f3: Four owner Cu/Zn labels differ from current canonical spelling

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: m763-copper-zinc-canonical-labels.

The maintained trace stock has two CHEBI:86318 slots labelled copper dichloride dihydrate and two CHEBI:49976 slots labelled zinc chloride. Current canonical labels are copper(II) chloride dihydrate and zinc dichloride. Both IDs remain compatible with the supplied formulas; this is label correspondence, not a wrong chemical identity. The four analogous slots in excluded CultureMech:003081 are context only.

### f4: Repair only the affected named parent stock representations

major / open / confirmed; issue key: m763-scoped-parent-stock-grounding.

M288 ingredients[17] and [18] map hexahydrate Co/Ni to anhydrous IDs; the receiving M763 owner already uses correct CHEBI:53503/53542 and must retain them. M288 HCl and M431 Se/W quantities also have batch-unit errors, while M762 phosphate remains flattened. These are scoped dependency issues, not extra merged owners.

## Recommended Actions And Acceptance Checks

### a1

After resolving the owner basis issues below, regenerate from the current maintained owner while preserving the source-specific glucose variant and all named stock boundaries.

- Seven stock structures and source-specific preparation survive generation.
- Generated and owner quantities retain their distinct correction status.

### a2

Preserve all correct owner stock topology and supplied forms; represent exact batch inputs and literal unspecified percentages, correct unsupported rate notes and remove only unverified extra operating assertions.

- Every supported per-litre statement has its own explicit basis.
- Glucose strength and 100 ml/L dose remain supported.
- No parent final-volume or percentage basis is inferred.

### a3

Update only the maintained owner primary/secondary labels at solutions[0].composition[7] and [8] to the exact pinned canonical labels, preserving the IDs and source forms.

- All four active owner label slots agree with current canonical metadata.
- No chemical-ID change or excluded-parent change is implied.

### a4

Correct the exact affected dependency members with original batch units and supplied forms; preserve the receiving owner’s correct hydrate IDs and all excluded parent formulations.

- Dependency Co/Ni hydrate IDs and HCl/Se/W original units match sources.
- Only the named trace, Se/W and phosphate subrecipes transfer.

    : {\n        \"iri\": \"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_176843\",\n     \
    \   \"lang\": \"en\",\n        \"description\": [\n          \"Any member of a\
    \ group of cobalamin vitamers that exhibit biological activity against vitamin\
    \ B<small><sub>12</sub></small> deficiency. Vitamin B<small><sub>12</sub></small>\
    \ deficiency is associated with low red blood cell count and anemia. The vitamers\
    \ are found in foods such as cereals, meat, fish, and poultry. The vitamers include\
    \ adenosylcobalamin, hydroxocobalamin, cyanocobalamin, aquacobalamin, nitritocobalamin\
    \ and methylcobabalamin (also includes their ionized, salt and phosphate derivatives).\"\
    \n        ],\n        \"synonyms\": [\n          \"vitamin B-12\",\n         \

    \  \"lang\": \"en\",\n        \"description\": [\n          \"<small>D</small>-Ribitol\
    \ in which the hydroxy group at position 5 is substituted by a 7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[<em>g</em>]pteridin-10(2<em>H</em>)-yl\
    \ moiety. It is a nutritional factor found in milk, eggs, malted barley, liver,\
    \ kidney, heart, and leafy vegetables, but the richest natural source is yeast.\
    \ The free form occurs only in the retina of the eye, in whey, and in urine; its\
    \ principal forms in tissues and cells are as flavin mononucleotide and flavin-adenine\
    \ dinucleotide.\"\n        ],\n        \"synonyms\": [\n          \"1-deoxy-1-(7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[g]pteridin-10(2H)-yl)-D-ribitol\"\

- assessment_id: ownership
  area: ownership
  topic: Repaired maintained owner and stale generated target
  outcome: concern
  summary: The sole maintained owner is TOGO M763. Its September repair adds seven
    populated stock structures, correct source-specific hydrate IDs and staged preparation;
    the generated August target still has seven Unknown placeholders and older mass-labelled
    additions. The linked CultureMech:003081 JCM-derived record is related context,
    not a second owner. Preserve current repairs while revisiting their unsupported
    quantitative bases.
  target_ids:
  - CultureMech:010170
  evidence_ids:
  - record
  - owner-0
  - history-full
  - main
- assessment_id: glucose
  area: quantity
  topic: Explicit glucose variant scope
  outcome: supported
  summary: M763 comments[2] explicitly replaces 0.1 M L-sodium lactate with filter-sterilized
    0.1 M glucose at 100 ml/L. The maintained owner correctly retains that strength
    and dose. This explicit per-litre instruction does not establish a final-volume
    denominator for every other ingredient or stock.
  target_ids:
  - CultureMech:010170
  evidence_ids:
  - main
- assessment_id: preparation
  area: representation
  topic: Retained anaerobic ordering and bounded gaps
  outcome: concern
  summary: The maintained owner retains N2–CO2 80:20 v/v, sealed basal autoclaving,
    cooling and aseptic anaerobic stock additions; the target omits them. The source
    does not establish main incubation temperature, pH, pressure or autoclave duration.
    A pure-N2 sulfide-stock atmosphere and the owner statement that JCM 197 prints
    vitamins per litre are not supported by the scoped source wording.

  severity: major
  status: open
  certainty: confirmed
  title: Regenerated output must retain the maintained seven-stock repair
  description: The target still has empty Unknown stock compositions and mass-labelled
    additions, while the sole owner has seven populated stocks and preparation. Its
    generated resazurin 0.5 G_PER_L and water 830 G_PER_L also retain old units. The
    owner repair is real and must not be described as absent or flattened.

- finding_id: f3
  issue_key: m763-copper-zinc-canonical-labels
  category: grounding
  severity: minor
  status: open
  certainty: confirmed
  title: Four owner Cu/Zn labels differ from current canonical spelling
  description: The maintained trace stock has two CHEBI:86318 slots labelled copper
    dichloride dihydrate and two CHEBI:49976 slots labelled zinc chloride. Current
    canonical labels are copper(II) chloride dihydrate and zinc dichloride. Both IDs
    remain compatible with the supplied formulas; this is label correspondence, not
    a wrong chemical identity. The four analogous slots in excluded CultureMech:003081
    are context only.
  target_ids:
  - CultureMech:010170
  field_paths:
  - solutions[0].composition
  evidence_ids:

  description: M288 ingredients[17] and [18] map hexahydrate Co/Ni to anhydrous IDs;
    the receiving M763 owner already uses correct CHEBI:53503/53542 and must retain
    them. M288 HCl and M431 Se/W quantities also have batch-unit errors, while M762
    phosphate remains flattened. These are scoped dependency issues, not extra merged
    owners.
